faq.subtitle: Everything people ask us, saved in one place. Pick a topic or open a bite.

still_stuck.title: Still stuck?
still_stuck.body: A person reads every email, usually within two working days. Tell us what you did, what you expected and what happened instead.

what.a: A place to save anything — websites, images, movies, games, notes — and find it again without doing the filing yourself. Save with one click and WebBites tags and organises it using AI, then searches by title, colour, tags and even the text on the page.

platforms.q: Which platforms does it run on?
platforms.a: The web app, native apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Vision Pro, Apple TV and Apple Watch, and a browser extension for saving from wherever you are. Everything syncs through your account.

account.q: Do I need an account to use the apps?
account.a: No. The apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Vision Pro work signed out, against a library kept on your own device, and nothing you save in that mode is sent to us. Sync, sharing, semantic search and the cloud features need an account, and you can switch the intelligence features to on-device models in Settings if you want to keep them local too. The details are in the Privacy Policy §2.

password.a: Use the reset page or the "Forgot password" link on the sign-in screen. The email arrives from our mail provider — check spam if it doesn't. If you signed in with Apple there is no password to reset: use the Apple button again.

sync.a: Check you're signed into the same account on both devices, then pull to refresh. A save made while offline sits in a queue and flushes when the network returns — the app shows those on the "Waiting to save" screen under Settings → Data & Offline. If something is stuck there for more than a few minutes with a working connection, email us.

extension.a: The extension saves through your signed-in session, so open the web app once and sign in, then try again. On Safari, extensions also need to be enabled and granted permission for the site you're on, in Safari → Settings → Extensions.

bad_save.q: A page saved badly — no image, wrong title, no article text
bad_save.a: Some sites block automated fetching, render everything in JavaScript, or sit behind a paywall or a login. In those cases we save what we can reach. Editing the title, description or image on the bite fixes it for good. Send us the URL if a site you care about consistently comes out wrong — a lot of them we can fix individually.

export.q: Can I export or import my bookmarks?
export.a: Both. Settings → Export, on any platform, gives you your library in a portable file, on any plan, at any time. To bring browser bookmarks in, follow the import guide.

pricing.a: There's a free plan, and paid plans for more bookmarks and the advanced features. The current plans and prices are on the pricing section of the home page.

cancel.q: How do I cancel or change my plan?
cancel.a: Cancel where you subscribed. If you subscribed on the web or on the Mac, it's Settings → Subscription, which opens the billing portal. If you subscribed through the App Store, it's in your Apple subscription settings on your device (Settings → your name → Subscriptions), because Apple bills those directly. You keep paid features until the end of the period you've paid for.

privacy.a: Your bookmarks are yours. We don't sell your data, and the apps can run entirely on-device if you never sign in. What we store, why, and for how long is spelled out in the Privacy Policy.

delete.q: How do I delete my account?
delete.a: Settings → Delete account, and confirm. It deletes your bookmarks, files and subscription along with it, and it is not reversible — so export first if you want a copy. No email to us is needed, and we don't put a retention offer in the way.

api.a: Yes — the developer page shows what it can do, and the documentation has the guides, your API keys, a playground and every endpoint.

legal.questions: Questions about this page? Write to {email}.

chat.title: Chat with us
chat.subtitle: A real person on our team picks this up — usually within two working days.
chat.not_configured: Chat isn't configured yet. Email us at {email}.
chat.sign_in_prompt: Sign in to start a conversation and keep your history in one place.

support.title: Support
support.subtitle: Something broken, something missing, or something you just can't find? Here's how to reach a person.
support.email_body: One person reads this address, usually within two working days. Tell us what you did, what you expected and what happened instead — and which app (web, iPhone, iPad, Mac, Vision Pro, TV, Watch or the browser extension) and version you were on. A screenshot saves a whole exchange.
support.row_bug: Report a bug or ask for help
support.row_feature: Request a feature, or vote on one
support.faq_body: Passwords, syncing, exports, cancelling, the extension and more are on the {link}.
support.security_body: Email {email} with "Security" in the subject and enough detail to reproduce the problem. Please don't publish it before we've had a chance to fix it, don't access or modify other people's data while testing, and don't run load or denial-of-service tests against the service. We'll confirm we've received it, keep you posted, and credit you when it's fixed if you'd like that.

support_chat.email_note: We only use it to reply. Your draft stays on this device.
support_chat.we_reply_to: We reply to {email} — usually within two working days.

export_guide.title: How to Export Your Bookmarks
export_guide.intro: Ready to bring your bookmarks to WebBites? Follow these simple instructions to export your bookmarks from your favorite browser.
export_guide.help_text: If you're having trouble exporting your bookmarks, feel free to {link}.
export_guide.next_intro: Now that you've exported your bookmarks, you can import them into WebBites:
export_guide.next_1: Go to your WebBites dashboard and open the settings modal.
export_guide.next_3: Select and upload your exported bookmarks file
export_guide.next_4: Select the ones you want to upload, click on 'Import' and let WebBites organize everything for you!

chrome_1.title: Open the Chrome Menu
chrome_1.description: Click on the three dots ⋮ in the top-right corner of your browser window to open the Chrome menu.

chrome_2.title: Access Bookmarks Manager
chrome_2.description: Navigate to Bookmarks > Bookmark Manager, or simply press Ctrl+Shift+O (Windows/Linux) or ⌘+Option+B (Mac).

chrome_3.title: Export Bookmarks
chrome_3.description: Click on the three dots ⋮ in the top-right corner of the Bookmark Manager, then select Export bookmarks.

chrome_4.title: Save the HTML File
chrome_4.description: Choose a location on your computer to save the HTML file containing your bookmarks. The default name will be something like 'bookmarks_[date].html'.
chrome_4.note: This HTML file contains all your bookmarks and their folder structure.

firefox_1.title: Open the Firefox Menu
firefox_1.description: Click on the three horizontal lines (hamburger menu) ☰ in the top-right corner of your browser window.

firefox_2.title: Access Bookmarks
firefox_2.description: Navigate to Bookmarks > Manage Bookmarks, or press Ctrl+Shift+B (Windows/Linux) or ⌘+Shift+B (Mac).

firefox_3.title: Export Bookmarks
firefox_3.description: In the Library window that opens, click on Import and Backup > Export Bookmarks to HTML.

firefox_4.title: Save the HTML File
firefox_4.description: Choose a location on your computer to save the HTML file. The default name will be 'bookmarks.html'.
firefox_4.note: Make sure to remember where you saved this file for easy access when importing to WebBites.

safari_1.title: Open Safari Menu
safari_1.description: Click on File in the top menu bar of Safari.

safari_2.title: Export Bookmarks
safari_2.description: Select Export Bookmarks from the dropdown menu.

safari_3.title: Save the File
safari_3.description: Choose a location on your Mac to save the bookmarks file. This will save a .zip file, you'll need to unzip it to get the .html file.
safari_3.note: Safari exports all your bookmarks, including those in the Favorites bar and all folders.

edge_1.title: Open Edge Menu
edge_1.description: Click on the three dots ⋯ in the top-right corner of your browser window, then click on Favorites.

edge_3.title: Save the HTML File
edge_3.description: Choose a location on your computer to save the HTML file containing your favorites/bookmarks.
edge_3.note: Edge will export all your favorites, including those in any folders you've created.

opera_1.title: Access Bookmarks
opera_1.description: Press Ctrl+Shift+B (Windows/Linux) or ⌘+Option+B (Mac) to open the Bookmark Manager, or click on the Opera menu and select Bookmarks > Bookmarks.

opera_3.title: Export Bookmarks
opera_3.description: Click on the Import/Export button in the bottom-left corner of the Bookmark Manager, then select Export bookmarks as HTML file.

opera_4.title: Save the HTML File
opera_4.description: Choose a location on your computer to save the HTML file containing your bookmarks.
opera_4.note: Opera's bookmark export includes all your bookmarks and their folder structure.

arc_1.title: Open Arc Sidebar
arc_1.description: Open the command bar by pressing ⌘+T, and go to arc://bookmarks.

arc_2.title: Export Bookmarks
arc_2.description: Click on the three dots ⋯ in the top-right corner of the Bookmarks panel, then select Settings. In the settings menu, find and click on Export Bookmarks.

arc_3.title: Save the HTML File
arc_3.description: Choose a location on your computer to save the HTML file containing your bookmarks.
arc_3.note: This HTML file contains all your bookmarks and their folder structure.

raindrop_1.title: Log into Raindrop.io
raindrop_1.description: Go to app.raindrop.io and log into your account.

raindrop_2.title: Access Settings
raindrop_2.description: Click on your profile picture in the top-right corner, then select Settings from the dropdown menu.

raindrop_3.title: Export Bookmarks
raindrop_3.description: In the Settings menu, navigate to the Backup tab. Under the 'Export' section, select your preferred format (HTML is recommended for WebBites compatibility).

raindrop_4.title: Download Your Bookmarks
raindrop_4.description: Click the Export button to generate and download your bookmarks file.
raindrop_4.note: Raindrop.io allows you to export in multiple formats, but HTML format works best for importing into WebBites.

intro.title: Your library for the web

ai.title: Organised for you
ai.description: Every bookmark is tagged and sorted as you save it. No folders to keep tidy.

search.title: Find it again
search.description: Search the words on the page, tags, notes, text inside images, even colour.

screenshots.title: Kept for good
screenshots.description: A full-page screenshot and a readable copy of every page, in case the original changes or disappears.

media.title: Save anything
media.description: Articles, images, videos, films, games and notes, side by side in one library.

ai_organisation.description: Automatically categorise and tag your bookmarks using advanced AI.

cross_platform.description: iPhone, iPad, Mac and the web, all showing the same library once you sign in.

reader.title: Reader mode
reader.description: Articles will automatically be formatted for better reading experience, even those behind paywalls!

raycast.title: Raycast ready
raycast.description: With our Raycast extension, all your bookmarks are just one keystroke away!

browsers.title: Save from your browser
browsers.description: One click with the Chrome extension, or the Safari extension that comes with the Mac and iPhone apps.

colors.title: Extract colors
colors.description: The main colors of all your bookmarks are extracted for you, making it possible to search by color!

tts.title: Text to speech
tts.description: Listen to anything you've saved, or any article from your feeds.

annotate.title: Annotate screenshots
annotate.description: Click anywhere on the screenshot to add an annotation.

ocr.title: OCR
ocr.description: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) will be applied to all images saved, making it possible to search them by text.

pin.title: Pin your bookmarks
pin.description: Pin your bookmarks to the top of your list for easy access.

save_anything.sentence: Save anything, from {websites}{images}{movies}{games} and even {notes} with our Notion-like editor.

roadmap_more.title: Plus many more!
roadmap_more.description: More features are always being added, check out the feedback board to see what's coming next!

developers.title: An API for everything you save
developers.description: Everything WebBites does, it does over HTTP. Save a link, search your library, get a webhook the moment the AI has finished with it.

rest.title: Plain REST
rest.text: An OpenAPI schema and a browser playground to try every call before you write any code.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.text: Point a URL at WebBites and it POSTs the finished bookmark — screenshot, summary and tags — signed so you can verify it.

keys.title: Your keys, your limits
keys.text: Create keys, see what each one has spent, and read the rate limit off every response header.

feeds.title: Follow the sites you love
feeds.description: A built-in reader for blogs, news and newsletters, with no algorithm. Read, listen to or summarise each article, and save the best to your library.
feeds.image_alt: The WebBites feed reader on a Mac, with feeds in the sidebar and an article open beside them

where.title: Where your library lives
where.separate: A WebBites account syncs everywhere. A device library stays on your iPhone, iPad or Mac, with no account at all. The two are separate: a device library never shows up on the web or in an account, and purchases don't carry over between them.
where.account_when: if you use the web or Chrome, or want feeds, AI tags and summaries.
where.device_when: if you only use Apple devices and want nothing on anyone's server.
